core_obligations: Embed an injective object into M-underlined, split it off, and conclude it is I(A)-underlined (proof lines 2963-2968).
Show that I(A) is pure injective using that universally exact sequences give exact sequences of functors (proof lines 2969-2973).
Conversely embed I-underlined into an injective J, identify J as I'-underlined with I' pure injective (proof lines 2976-2981).
Use injectivity of the map of functors to get universal injectivity of I -> I', split by purity, and conclude that I-underlined is injective (proof lines 2982-2985).
proof_roadmap: Every injective object is a pure injective module (proof lines 2963-2973).
Every pure injective module gives an injective object (proof lines 2976-2985).
difficulty_reason: For a ring A, the lemma identifies the injective objects of the category A of adequate functors on Alg_A with the functors I-underlined for pure injective modules I (statement lines 2954-2959). The proof runs in two directions: an injective object I is embedded into some M-underlined, injectivity makes M-underlined a direct sum I + F, evaluation at A splits the module and gives I = I(A)-underlined, and the module I(A) is then shown to be pure injective because universally exact sequences of modules give exact sequences of adequate functors; conversely, a pure injective module I is embedded into an injective object J of A, the first direction shows J = I'-underlined with I' pure injective, injectivity of the map of modules follows from injectivity of the map of functors, and purity of I makes it split, so I-underlined is a summand of an injective object and hence injective (proof lines 2962-2985). The level is H3: both directions are argued with the evaluation functor and the splitting step displayed.
